stages.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. High-fidelity IMAGEGEN visual layout exploration, not HTML or implemented UI. One layout concept only.
Image 1 is the earlier component reference, to REDESIGN with the new hierarchy below. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL Software logo. Image 3 is the ORIGINAL Consulting logo. Preserve both flower emblems and exact wordmark letterforms, with no newly invented logos. Original logo serif weight is fixed; all newly designed serif headings use NORMAL/BOOK weight. Refined light sans-serif navigation/body text. English copy.
Magazine polish: an underlying alignment grid, substantial whitespace, fine paper grain, restrained typography. The Software palette is cool teal, lagoon and frost; Consulting uses berry/mulberry and low-chroma linen, never bubblegum pink. The latest request explicitly ALLOWS broad COLOR SURFACES in the FOOTER and more color in the header. Do not inherit the old all-white footer constraint. No browser chrome, photos, landscape illustrations, maps, giant page headlines, fake claims, ornament-only eyebrow labels, explanations, measurements, arrows pointing to layout features, device mockups or comparison grids of unrelated designs.
HEADER CONCEPT: Show TWO desktop page excerpts stacked vertically on ONE wide landscape sheet, around 2000 x 1050, documenting TWO STATES OF THE SAME HEADER LAYOUT, not two alternative ideas. Upper excerpt is on Software; lower excerpt is on Consulting. Large blank separation between the excerpts. Both headers have IDENTICAL spatial arrangement and geometry. Preserve the compact scale of image 1: each toolbar is only 48 CSS pixels high at a 1440px viewport, i.e. its raster height is about 3.3% of this sheet's width. Logos roughly 20 CSS pixels tall, navigation 14-15px, no tall masthead and no stacked nav rows.
Critical information hierarchy: The CURRENT SITE owns one coherent unit, in this order: current-site wordmark -> its own area navigation -> "EN / DE". The language switch MUST be INSIDE that current-site unit and BEFORE the separate sister-site link. It must never sit behind the sister brand, seem attached to the other site, or appear twice.
Software state: original Software wordmark as current logo; ONLY local links "Products", "Open Source", "Agents & Skills"; THEN "EN / DE". Separately, at the far right beyond a clear gap or boundary, show a small original berry Consulting emblem with text "Consulting ↗" as a SINGLE cross-site entry. NO Services, Profiles or References in the Software-state toolbar.
Consulting state: original Consulting wordmark as current logo; ONLY local links "Services", "Profiles", "References"; THEN "EN / DE". Separately, at the same far-right position beyond the same gap/boundary, show a small original teal Software emblem with text "Software ↗" as the SINGLE cross-site entry. NO Products, Open Source or Agents & Skills in the Consulting-state toolbar.
The sister-site entry is visibly secondary in scale and treatment. Never place both full wordmarks next to each other in the local navigation; never weave the other brand into local links. Main current-site unit uses about 82-86% of row width, sister entry the last 14-18%. Language has a stable position near the end of the MAIN unit; the separate sister entry starts AFTER it.
Below each header only a small, modest 28 CSS-pixel regular-serif page line for context: upper "Products, open source and agent tools."; lower "Architecture and engineering for complex web applications." Leave the rest quiet paper. No newsletter or footer or navigation explanations in this image.
Layout H01: A SOFT COLORED LOCAL ZONE. The main current-site unit is one flat 48px area filled with pale Software frost in the upper state, pale low-chroma Consulting linen in the lower state. Current wordmark and local links share its baseline. EN / DE sits at its rightmost end. A 24px white gap then separates the sister-site entry, which is plain small original emblem + text on white paper, no surrounding button. Main unit may have a 4px radius at its right end only. The color area itself clearly tells you where you are; the other site sits OUTSIDE it. No full paired-brand masthead.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: desktop header layout study, two current-site states of one layout.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is the complete ORIGINAL Sebastian/Software logo. Image 3 is the complete ORIGINAL Sebastian/Consulting logo.
Primary request: Refine this existing layout for compact proportions and COMPLETE brand wordmarks. Keep the original distinct design idea, colors, white page context, two vertically separated states, all current-site navigation wording, hierarchy, positions and typography style.
Required logo correction: In BOTH rows EVERY logo, including the sibling website link, must use the ENTIRE supplied lockup: emblem plus exact full text "Sebastian/SOFTWARE" or "Sebastian/CONSULTING". Preserve the slash and original letterform arrangement. Never abbreviate to "Software" or "Consulting". Never omit "Sebastian/" from the sister link. Do not redraw the emblem or crop logos. A small outward arrow may sit AFTER the complete lockup. Color inversion to ivory on colored surfaces is permitted without changing geometry.
Scale correction: Keep the same wide canvas, approximately 1730 by 910 pixels. Each horizontal header surface must be ONLY 58 raster pixels high, corresponding to 48 CSS pixels at a 1440px desktop viewport. Current and sibling complete logo artwork is about 30 raster pixels high, nav text only 18 raster pixels, language text 18 raster pixels; center all vertically in the 58px strip. Shrink both artwork AND vertical padding from the oversized target. Do not leave the current 85-95px header height.
Floating placement: Keep the entire composition inset with at least 5% white margin on BOTH sides and visible white air above each header. No edge-to-edge screen bands. No drop shadows, no 3D, no gradient. Retain the soft tinted local bar with its rounded trailing end.
Horizontal geometry: Give about 76% of the usable width to the current brand, local navigation and language as ONE group. After a clear gap/boundary, use the final 20% for the complete sibling lockup. The sibling lockup can be slightly smaller, still fully legible and complete. Prefer tighter sensible horizontal gaps inside the local navigation rather than truncating a logo. Never move the language into the sibling zone.
Top state: full Sebastian/SOFTWARE logo; ONLY "Products", "Open Source", "Agents & Skills"; "EN / DE"; clear boundary; full Sebastian/CONSULTING logo with outward arrow.
Bottom state: full Sebastian/CONSULTING logo; ONLY "Services", "Profiles", "References"; "EN / DE"; clear boundary; full Sebastian/SOFTWARE logo with outward arrow.
Keep the same exact two regular-weight serif context sentences beneath the headers. Do not add footer, submenus, more navigation, measurements, captions, explanatory labels or decorative illustrations. Other than the logo completion, compact scaling and inset treatment, preserve the concept.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Change ONLY the vertical scale of the two navigation strips in this image. Both currently look around 80px high and are too thick. Redraw each strip at 58px total height on this same 1730px-wide canvas, including its padding and corners. This means physically reduce the filled/outlined surface height by approximately one third, not just the text. Keep each strip's vertical center and horizontal left/right positions. Center much SMALLER entire logo lockups in the thinner strip: every full Sebastian/SOFTWARE and Sebastian/CONSULTING logo is only 28px high. Navigation and EN / DE are 18px high. The existing shapes, palettes, two states, full unabridged logos WITH SLASH, separate sibling link, all wording, body headings, white margins and background must remain identical. The design target is a discreet 48-CSS-pixel desktop bar, not an oversized header. Do not make any logo partial, omit Sebastian/, move the language or add anything. No size labels or measurements visible.
